title: Remediation SLA mapping (TTM/TTR) by incident category, severity, and customer tier
author: Aisha Bello
content:
## Purpose
This page defines Redwood Inference’s **remediation SLAs** for production incidents, expressed as:
- **TTM (Time to Mitigate):** time from incident declaration (or first on-call page, whichever is earlier) to stopping active customer impact (e.g., rollback, reroute, degraded mode, scaling, traffic shaping).
- **TTR (Time to Permanent Fix):** time to ship a verified fix that prevents recurrence of the same failure mode (code/config change deployed, capacity change completed, or hardware remediation completed). For cross-team issues, the *primary owner* is accountable for driving the fix to completion.

This mapping is used by:
- Incident Command (IC) for expectations and escalation
- Support/CS for customer updates and ETAs
- Postmortems for tracking action item due dates
- Reporting for MTTR/TTM trends by category/owner/tier

## Scope
Applies to **production incidents** across:
- **Hosted API** and **Dedicated pools**
- **Private deployments** where Redwood is the primary operator for day-2 operations

Security incidents follow the Security IR process. If a security incident results in service impact, use this page for mitigation timing *in addition to* Security IR requirements.

## Customer tiers (for remediation targets)
Use the **highest impacted tier**.

| Tier | Definition | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **Tier 1 (Enterprise / SLA-backed)** | Contractual SLA or Dedicated/Private commit. Named account; Customer Success owner; typically requires proactive comms. | Dedicated pools, Private (Redwood-operated), Hosted Enterprise |
| **Tier 2 (Paid / Business)** | Paid self-serve or annual plan without custom SLA; support via normal channels; comms usually via status page + ticket updates. | Hosted “Business/Pro” |
| **Tier 3 (Dev / Free / Internal)** | Free, trial, or internal-only environments; comms are best-effort unless broadly impacting platform stability. | Free credits, sandbox projects, internal test endpoints |

## Severity alignment (do not override)
Severity is defined by the standard incident severity policy. This page **does not change** severity criteria.

Operational shorthand:
- **Sev0:** critical widespread outage / major customer harm / multi-region or sustained platform unavailability
- **Sev1:** significant customer impact, partial outage, or severe degradation for a major segment
- **Sev2:** limited impact, degraded performance, or elevated errors with workarounds
- **Sev3:** minor impact, brief blips, or contained issues with minimal customer-facing effect

## Global escalation + communications expectations (baseline)
These expectations apply regardless of category; category-specific notes follow in the SLA tables.

| Severity | Paging + escalation expectations | Customer comms expectations (baseline) | Post-incident follow-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sev0** | IC + SRE on-call immediately. Page owning Eng on-call within 5 min. Page Platform sponsor + SRE sponsor within 15 min. | Status page update within 15 min (initial). Enterprise proactive outreach within 30 min. Updates every 30 min until mitigated. | Postmortem required. Exec summary required. Action items tracked with due dates. |
| **Sev1** | IC + SRE on-call. Page owning Eng on-call within 10 min. Escalate to sponsor if not progressing within 30 min. | Status page update within 30 min if customer-visible. Enterprise outreach within 60 min. Updates every 60 min until mitigated. | Postmortem required. |
| **Sev2** | Owning Eng on-call + SRE as needed. Escalate if multiple customers/tier1 affected. | Ticket updates for impacted customers; status page if broad. Updates every business day (or sooner if changing). | Postmortem required if Tier 1 impacted or if recurrence risk is high; otherwise lightweight write-up. |
| **Sev3** | Handle in on-call queue or normal sprint workflow. | Usually no broadcast; respond on request. | Optional retro; required if repeated (>=3 similar events in 30 days) or if indicates systemic gap. |

## How to use this mapping during an incident
1) Set **Incident Category (v1)** as early as possible (goal: within 15 minutes of declaration). If uncertain, pick best-fit; reclassify after mitigation.
2) Set **Customer Tier (highest impacted)** and **Impacted Surface**.
3) Use the relevant category table below to determine:
   - Target **TTM** and **TTR** for the incident
   - Required escalations
   - Postmortem + action item expectations

## Notes on measurement
- Start time: first page to #oncall / PD trigger / incident declare timestamp (use earliest).
- TTM ends when impact is stopped (error rate/latency returns under SLO or traffic is safely shed with communicated degraded mode).
- TTR ends when fix is deployed and validated (or capacity/hardware remediation completed) with evidence linked in postmortem.

---

# SLA tables by incident category (taxonomy v1)
The tables below define target TTM/TTR by **Severity x Tier** for each category, plus **category-specific escalation** and **follow-up requirements**.

## Category: Routing / Smart-routing / Policy
Examples: routing rule regression, regional routing loop, policy engine rejecting valid traffic, fallback policy misfire.

| Severity | Tier 1 TTM / TTR | Tier 2 TTM / TTR | Tier 3 TTM / TTR | Escalation notes | Follow-up requirements |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sev0** | **30m / 48h** | 45m / 72h | 60m / 5bd | Page **Platform Routing** on-call immediately. If mitigation not found in 20m, page **Control Plane** + **Infra** for capacity/reroute support. | Postmortem required. Add regression test/eval or policy validation gate if change-induced. |
| **Sev1** | **60m / 5bd** | 90m / 7bd | 2h / 10bd | Escalate to Platform sponsor if still user-impacting after 60m. | Postmortem required for Tier 1; recommended otherwise if change-induced. |
| **Sev2** | **4h / 10bd** | 8h / 15bd | 2bd / 20bd | If recurring, create routing SLO alert or guardrail task. | Retro required for Tier 1; otherwise ticket with clear owner + due date. |
| **Sev3** | **2bd / 20bd** | 5bd / 30bd | Best-effort / Backlog | Use normal sprint unless risk of escalation. | Track as bug; add to monthly taxonomy review if recurring. |

## Category: Capacity Exhaustion / Autoscaling / Scheduler Saturation
Examples: dedicated pool saturation, queue depth runaway, autoscaler misconfigured, GPU pool underprovisioned, scheduler headroom bug.

| Severity | Tier 1 TTM / TTR | Tier 2 TTM / TTR | Tier 3 TTM / TTR | Escalation notes | Follow-up requirements |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sev0** | **30m / 72h** | 45m / 5bd | 60m / 7bd | Page **Infra/Fleet** + **Runtime Scheduling** immediately. If Tier 1 Dedicated/Private, page **CS owner** for comms coordination. | Postmortem required. Add capacity model update + alert thresholds; document new headroom target. |
| **Sev1** | **60m / 7bd** | 90m / 10bd | 2h / 15bd | If scaling actions require cloud quota/vendor, escalate to Infra manager on-call within 2h. | Postmortem required for Tier 1; include updated runbook + autoscaling guardrails. |
| **Sev2** | **8h / 15bd** | 2bd / 20bd | 5bd / 30bd | Consider proactive customer guidance (rate limits / batching) if demand-driven. | Retro required for Tier 1 Dedicated; otherwise bug + capacity plan task. |
| **Sev3** | **5bd / 30bd** | Best-effort / Backlog | Best-effort / Backlog | Track in capacity planning board. | Optional retro if repeated or if impacts forecast accuracy. |

## Category: Runtime Crash / Kernel Regression / Model-serving Instability
Examples: inference worker crash loop, CUDA OOM due to regression, kernel mismatch, model-specific instability after upgrade.

| Severity | Tier 1 TTM / TTR | Tier 2 TTM / TTR | Tier 3 TTM / TTR | Escalation notes | Follow-up requirements |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sev0** | **30m / 48h** | 45m / 72h | 60m / 5bd | Page **Runtime** on-call immediately. If mitigation not found in 20m, force rollback/canary halt and engage **SRE** for safe traffic drains. | Postmortem required. Add canary signal and rollback automation if missing. |
| **Sev1** | **60m / 5bd** | 90m / 7bd | 2h / 10bd | Escalate to Runtime sponsor if persistent after 2h or if crash is nondeterministic. | Postmortem required for Tier 1; include repro + test coverage gap analysis. |
| **Sev2** | **8h / 10bd** | 2bd / 15bd | 5bd / 20bd | If model-specific, ensure model catalog owner is tagged and rollout paused. | Retro required for Tier 1; otherwise ticket + validate monitoring. |
| **Sev3** | **5bd / 20bd** | Best-effort / Backlog | Best-effort / Backlog | Bundle into next runtime patch if safe. | Optional retro if repeated. |

## Category: Edge / Gateway / Streaming Transport
Examples: streaming disconnects, gateway overload, TLS handshake failures, HTTP/2 issues, request parsing regression.

| Severity | Tier 1 TTM / TTR | Tier 2 TTM / TTR | Tier 3 TTM / TTR | Escalation notes | Follow-up requirements |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sev0** | **30m / 72h** | 45m / 5bd | 60m / 7bd | Page **Infra/Networking** and **Platform (API Gateway)** immediately. If region-specific, engage regional failover/reroute early. | Postmortem required. Include load test or synthetic monitoring gaps. |
| **Sev1** | **60m / 7bd** | 90m / 10bd | 2h / 15bd | If streaming-only, ensure comms specify workaround (non-streaming, smaller chunks). | Postmortem required for Tier 1; add client guidance + SDK mitigation if applicable. |
| **Sev2** | **8h / 15bd** | 2bd / 20bd | 5bd / 30bd | If tied to specific SDK version, coordinate with DevEx for advisory. | Retro required for Tier 1; otherwise ticket with owner. |
| **Sev3** | **5bd / 30bd** | Best-effort / Backlog | Best-effort / Backlog | Handle via normal backlog. | Optional. |

## Category: Control Plane / Auth / Quotas / Account Configuration
Examples: auth outage, token verification failures, quota enforcement bug, project routing misconfig from console, deploy/rollout controller issue.

| Severity | Tier 1 TTM / TTR | Tier 2 TTM / TTR | Tier 3 TTM / TTR | Escalation notes | Follow-up requirements |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sev0** | **30m / 48h** | 45m / 72h | 60m / 5bd | Page **Platform Control Plane** immediately. If auth is impacted, page **Security on-call** for coordination (even if not security incident). | Postmortem required. Validate auth/runbook and add circuit breakers/fail-open policy if approved. |
| **Sev1** | **60m / 5bd** | 90m / 7bd | 2h / 10bd | Escalate to Platform sponsor if not mitigated in 90m. | Postmortem required for Tier 1; otherwise recommended. |
| **Sev2** | **8h / 10bd** | 2bd / 15bd | 5bd / 20bd | If misconfig affects single customer, consider Support-led mitigation with Eng consult (but still track SLA). | Retro required for Tier 1; otherwise ticket + SOP update. |
| **Sev3** | **5bd / 20bd** | Best-effort / Backlog | Best-effort / Backlog | Normal backlog. | Optional. |

## Category: Fleet / GPU Hardware / Cloud Provider Dependency
Examples: GPU host failures above baseline, driver issues, provider outage/maintenance, multi-node cluster impairment.

| Severity | Tier 1 TTM / TTR | Tier 2 TTM / TTR | Tier 3 TTM / TTR | Escalation notes | Follow-up requirements |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sev0** | **30m / 5bd** | 45m / 7bd | 60m / 10bd | Page **Infra/Fleet** immediately. If provider dependency, open vendor ticket within 15m and attach to incident. Prioritize failover/reroute. | Postmortem required. Include vendor RCA tracking and long-term mitigation (multi-region, spare capacity). |
| **Sev1** | **60m / 7bd** | 90m / 10bd | 2h / 15bd | If Tier 1 Dedicated impacted, page account CS within 60m with interim ETA. | Postmortem required for Tier 1; otherwise recommended if vendor-related. |
| **Sev2** | **8h / 20bd** | 2bd / 30bd | 5bd / 45bd | Hardware remediation can be longer; focus on mitigation via draining/evac. | Retro required for Tier 1; otherwise ticket + capacity risk note. |
| **Sev3** | **5bd / 45bd** | Best-effort / Backlog | Best-effort / Backlog | Track in fleet reliability queue. | Optional. |

## Category: Observability / Telemetry Pipeline (Impacting SLO Attainment)
Examples: missing metrics/logs/traces preventing detection/mitigation; alerting failure leading to delayed response.

Important: Observability-only issues that do **not** impact production service performance are typically **Sev3**. If they impede incident response for Tier 1 workloads, treat as higher severity per policy.

| Severity | Tier 1 TTM / TTR | Tier 2 TTM / TTR | Tier 3 TTM / TTR | Escalation notes | Follow-up requirements |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sev0** | **60m / 7bd** | 90m / 10bd | 2h / 15bd | Page **Observability** immediately if blind during Sev0/Sev1. Prioritize restoring minimal golden signals + paging. | Postmortem required. Must include “detection gap” section and alert remediation. |
| **Sev1** | **2h / 10bd** | 4h / 15bd | 8h / 20bd | Escalate if alerting failure caused delayed mitigation. | Postmortem required for Tier 1; otherwise retro if materially impacted response. |
| **Sev2** | **1bd / 20bd** | 2bd / 30bd | 5bd / 45bd | Schedule fixes with clear owner and validation plan. | Ticket required; retro if recurring. |
| **Sev3** | **5bd / 45bd** | Best-effort / Backlog | Best-effort / Backlog | Normal backlog. | Optional. |

---

# Cross-cutting rules (apply to all categories)
## 1) If mitigation exceeds target
If TTM target is exceeded (or projected to be exceeded):
- IC must explicitly call out “**TTM at risk**” in the incident channel and assign an owner to mitigation strategy.
- Page the category owner’s **manager-on-call/sponsor** per the baseline table.
- Ensure Support/CS has an updated ETA and workaround guidance.

## 2) Permanent fix accountability
- The **primary category owner** is accountable for driving TTR, even if work spans teams.
- If the fix requires product decision (e.g., changing default behavior), create a tracking ticket and tag **Product alignment** (Marissa Cole / Lauren Bishop) for sign-off.

## 3) Postmortem due dates (minimums)
- Sev0: draft within **2 business days**, finalized within **5 business days**
- Sev1: draft within **5 business days**, finalized within **10 business days**
- Sev2: draft within **10 business days** (if required), finalized within **15 business days**
- Sev3: optional

## 4) Customer communication artifacts
For Tier 1 incidents (any Sev0–Sev2):
- Ensure Support/CS has: summary, impacted surfaces, mitigations, workaround, next update time.
- For Dedicated/Private: include region/pool identifier and whether headroom was impacted.

## 5) Exceptions
Exceptions to these targets must be recorded in the incident timeline and postmortem with:
- why the SLA was not achievable
- what was done to mitigate customer impact
- updated plan and owner for TTR

---

# Change management
This mapping is versioned with taxonomy v1. Proposed changes require review from:
- SRE sponsor (Sean Gallagher)
- Platform sponsor (Priya Natarajan)
- Support escalation owner (Dev Patel) for comms impact

Update cadence: reviewed monthly in the incident taxonomy review meeting; emergency updates allowed if required for operational correctness.
